Change c0408. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. IV; 1831 Ch. XXI.

Context before (unchanged): Persecuted and tortured as I am and have been, can death be any evil to me?"

1818 text: "Nothing indeed could be more unfortunate and agonizing than the strange chances that have lately occurred. You were thrown, by some surprising accident, on this shore, renowned for its hospitality: seized immediately, and charged with murder.

1831 text: "Nothing indeed could be more unfortunate and agonising than the strange chances that have lately occurred. You were thrown, by some surprising accident, on this shore, renowned for its hospitality; seized immediately, and charged with murder.

Diff: " Nothing indeed could be more unfortunate and [-agonizing-] {+agonising+} than the strange chances that have lately occurred. You were thrown, by some surprising accident, on this shore, renowned for its hospitality [-:-] {+;+} seized immediately, and charged with murder.

Context after (unchanged): The first sight that was presented to your eyes was the body of your friend, murdered in so unaccountable a manner, and placed, as it were, by some fiend across your path."

result.rationale: Main change is orthographic: 'agonizing' becomes 'agonising' (-ize to -ise). The colon-to-semicolon swap after 'hospitality' is punctuation only, not a wording change, so it is a minor secondary note.
